Lessons.Title: Hours, Minutes, and Seconds
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will use multiplication to describe the relationship between units of time and to express larger units of time in terms of smaller ones.
In grade 2, you learned to tell time to the nearest five minutes and recognized that there are 60 minutes in 1 hour. In grade 3, you learned to tell time to the nearest minute and to measure intervals of time. You may also know that there are 60 seconds in a minute.
Core relationship: Hours, minutes and seconds. Use 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  What Do You Know about 1 Hour?	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Mai’s School Day	 (20 minutes); Activity 2:  Precious Minutes and Seconds	 (15 minutes); Cool-down:  Time on Chores	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: How many minutes are in 2 hours and 15 minutes?
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): How many seconds are in 3 minutes?
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.

KeyConcepts.Title: Hours, minutes and seconds
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds.
KeyConcepts.Example: How many minutes are in 2 hours and 15 minutes?

KeyConcepts.Title: Converting parts of an hour
KeyConcepts.Definition: An hour is 60 minutes; fractional hours are corresponding fractions of 60 minutes.
KeyConcepts.Rule: One half hour is 30 minutes, three quarters of an hour is 45 minutes.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source-aligned mathematical model
WorkedExamples.Question: How many minutes are in 2 hours and 15 minutes?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds.
Steps: Identify all quantities and common units.
Confirm 135 by the inverse or a visual model.

WorkedExamples.Title: Mai's schedule: hours to minutes
WorkedExamples.Question: Mai spends 1 1/2 hours on homework and reading. How many minutes is that?
WorkedExamples.Method: Convert each part of the mixed hour into minutes.
WorkedExamples.Check: The 2021 described schedule contains this 1 1/2-hour activity.

WorkedExamples.Title: Diego's timer: minutes to seconds
WorkedExamples.Question: Diego allows 30 minutes for daily reading. How many seconds is that?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the stated conversion 1 minute=60 seconds.
Steps: Multiply 30 minutes by 60 seconds per minute.
WorkedExamples.Check: This uses the original teacher-activity conversion described in the source pack.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Reading 1 1/2 hours as 1 minute and 30 seconds.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A half-hour is 30 minutes, while a half-minute is 30 seconds.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Convert the stated whole unit before adding: 1 1/2 hours=90 minutes.

SummaryPoints: Independently authored first-party Cool-down; not original publisher item.
